title: Investigating a digital intervention for patients suffering from fibromyalgia: randomized controlled trial (libretti trial)
summary:
Fibromyalgia is a chronic condition. People with fibromyalgia often have pain in many parts of the body, tiredness, and sleep problems. Care from specialists is not always easy to reach.

This study asks whether an online program called dovalin helps adults with fibromyalgia when it is used in addition to the care they already receive. dovalin explains the condition and offers exercises for pain, tiredness, stress, sleep, movement, and everyday life. People use it on their own, on a computer, tablet, or phone, for six months.

About 306 adults will take part. A computer will assign each person by chance to one of two groups. One group can use dovalin straight away, together with their usual care. The other group keeps their usual care and can use dovalin after six months. Both groups receive the same written information about fibromyalgia and treatment options.

Everyone answers questionnaires before the start, after three months, and after six months. The main question is how much fibromyalgia affects daily life after three months. Further questions look at how people deal with pain, how confident they feel in managing the condition, and how anxious or low in mood they feel.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Male, female, or non-binary
- Fulfillment of diagnostic criteria for fibromyalgia (2016 revision)
- Diagnosis of fibromyalgia (ICD-10-GM M79.70), confirmed by a physician's letter or an equivalent comprehensive medical report
- Increased fibromyalgia impact (cut-off of ≥ 39 on the FIQ)
- Stable fibromyalgia-related treatment (medication, psychotherapy, physical therapy, or no treatment) for at least 30 days at the time of inclusion
- Presence of a stable, individually established rescue medication for pain, with confirmed patient commitment to use as needed
- Prior physician-delivered counseling regarding non-pharmacological strategies for the management of fibromyalgia
- Consent to participation
- Sufficient knowledge of the German language
- Basic IT skills necessary to use a digital intervention
Exclusion criteria:
- Plans to change fibromyalgia-related treatment (medication, psychotherapy, physical therapy) in the upcoming 3 months after inclusion
- Current intake of strong opioids (according to WHO step 3)
- Known somatic or psychiatric condition that might interfere with successful study participation, in particular: acute tumor disease with ongoing tumor-specific treatment; chronic lung disease with significantly impaired physical capacity; chronic inflammatory systemic disease with significantly impaired physical capacity; neurological disease with significantly impaired physical capacity or mobility; severe psychiatric disorder, in particular psychotic disorder, bipolar disorder, severe depressive episode, severe personality disorder, substance dependence, or acute suicidality
- Ongoing rehabilitation following surgical intervention
- Treating physician's suspicion of drug-induced fibromyalgia symptoms
- Ongoing efforts to obtain disability pension, other social benefits, or official recognition of severe disability due to fibromyalgia
- Previous use of any digital intervention for fibromyalgia (including dovalin) or another digital intervention developed by GAIA
